coarse._source: Rust-only figure: a bot outside the loaded window walks chunk to chunk toward the runner at the walking speed (4 m/s) and is placed on a dry open cell once its position is on the window floor

_intents_note: relay and pickup are still valid intent names, but the goal intent already takes every relay and useful item, so the standard list leaves them out

revive._source: Rust-only figures: a bot walks to a downed teammate (the runner or a bot) on its floor within range_factor times the follow radius, and stands within stand_fraction of the revive reach (data/revive.json) to hold the revive; a body with a hunter within safe_range metres of it (or where the bot remembers seeing one, flee.memory) is left until the hunter has gone

summon._source: Rust-only figure: owner summons stop once the room holds this many bots in all

threat._source: Godot npc_teammates.gd 25 THREAT_RANGE, 307 smart scale (.5 + smart/100), 324-326 running (the flight distance and away vector are in the 'flee' block); Rust raises the base so every smartness notices and flees sooner

hide._source: Rust-only figures: a bot hides when a chase is seen at the threat range, from a locker within 8 m, and comes out 3 s after no chaser is within 16 m

flee._cover_note: Rust-only figures: a flight cell that no hunter within sight_range has a clear line to counts cover_bonus metres farther than it is, so a bot ducks round a corner rather than run down the hunter's corridor (0 turns the rule off); one flight plan tests at most cover_checks cells for it. A bot remembers where it last saw a hunter for memory seconds and takes no goal, errand or revive within memory_radius metres of that point
flee._source: Rust-only figures: a bot sees a hunter of any state within 18 m, 70 degrees either side of its heading with a clear line, or within 4 m all round; a bot that heard a noise runs from a hunter within 20 m; its flight route keeps 3 m off every hunter, is at most 18 cells long, and is re-planned at most every 0.4 s when a hunter crosses it (also after a plan that found no route) and looks at 600 cells at most; a bot stays alarmed 3 s after it last saw or heard a hunter. Godot only flees a chasing hunter inside the threat range

errand._source: Rust-only figures: a relay or locker errand is taken within the leash of the runner, when no hunter is within safe_range of it

pickup._source: Rust-only figures: a bot takes a battery or stim pack within 10 m of the runner when the team has room; tools and other items are left lying

searched._source: Rust-only figures: the last 8 points hunters searched, and no errand spot within 4 m of one

doors._source: Rust-only figures: a bot is at a door within 1.5 m, and shuts it once 2.5 m clear of the threshold

door._source: Rust-only figures from the first port (npc.rs DOOR_THINK); no Godot line; shortened so bots clear doors faster at every smartness

water._source: Rust-only figure: a bot keeps out of sewer water at least this deep (metres over the bed) unless it is fleeing a chasing hunter

collision._source: Moved from npc.rs consts with the same values: bodies more than height metres apart in height do not collide; a bot is pushed out of an overlap by at most push_cap metres a frame and steers away at up to soft_speed m/s within soft_margin metres of touching. The landing offset is flights.json land_spread.

goals._source: Rust-only figures: a bot scores relays 100, a battery or heal item 70 while the lamp is under 30 percent or stamina under 35 percent, a useful pickup 40 and the exit 20 (once the level's relays are done), less 0.1 per path step up to 25, so a kind never loses to a lower one; a hunter-searched cell costs 12 steps; it picks again at most every 2 s (scaled faster by smart) and gives a goal up after 90 s; leash: a bot more than 36 m from the runner for 50 s drops its goal and takes none until it is back within 36 m. The follow intent stays last as the fallback. stuck (headless/bot.rs recovery ladder): after 2 s without moving 0.25 m a bot repaths, then presses a shut door within 2.5 m, then steps aside 0.6 s in a seeded direction, then gives the goal up for 20 s. The follow walk and the walk to a downed teammate use the same seconds, progress, door_reach and aside_seconds (repath, door, step aside, and again; no give-up)

life._nap_note: Rust-only (Godot teammates never sleep). A bot with nothing else to do may walk to a bed (hunter point of interest "bed") within range of the runner and lie on it for 20 to 40 s. It wakes when a hunter of its level is within wake_hunter_distance (seen or not), a chasing one is within wake_chase_distance, it hears a noise, another intent takes over, or the runner goes out of range. gap is the least seconds between two naps of one bot; a bed is not picked while a hunter is within hunter_clear_distance of the bot, within leader_clear_distance of the runner, or when another bot has it. The bot's position stays the stand cell beside the bed, so the wire is unchanged (a guest sees it standing); docs/SLEEP.md
life._source: Rust-only figures: when no hunter is near and no errand or goal applies, a bot acts like a player who has stopped to look about. It picks a point from the hunter points of interest (hunters/activities.rs: room centres, lockers, relays, doors) or stays where it is, walks there (sprint_burst runs), does an activity for a few seconds (look around, check a locker or a door, inspect a relay, idle, crouch, play an emote from data/player/emotes.json), then pauses. range is the farthest it goes from the runner; past it the follow intent walks it back and it resumes once it is back in follow range. Weights are relative; durations and pauses are [min, max] seconds.
life._return_note: return_distance 6.0 m and return_timeout 8 s are KT-pass picks (2026-11-08), not Godot figures: a bot past range walks back until it is within return_distance (and the follow range), and after return_timeout it follows plainly (follow_only) until it is back inside range. follow_only_timeout 10 s is also a KT-pass pick: a plain follow that has not closed in by goals.stuck.progress metres for that long is dropped with a fresh route, so follow_only never holds a bot that cannot route (bots have no teleport-to-runner rule)

lively._source: Rust-only figures (KT pass 2026-11-08): bots act like players. Each bot gets one personality at spawn from the weights (a hash of its name and slot, so a rebuild keeps it); acts multiplies the weight of the life acts the bot may pick (never adds one), the *_scale numbers scale the glance rate, the follow ring, the pause between activities, the idle fidget rate, the walk stops and the chance of a reply emote, and peek_chance is the chance a door check is done crouched. head: the head turns up to max_yaw degrees either side and max_pitch up or down at rate per second; a standing bot turns its body when the head would have to turn past body_over degrees; nod_* is the head nod while it chats. glance: a bot looks at a hunter it sees within range (clear line) for hold seconds, then waits gap seconds (shorter for a larger glance_scale), taking it with this chance. runner_look: a bot near its runner looks at it now and then. fidget: a standing bot with nothing to look at turns its head by up to yaw and pitch degrees for hold seconds every gap seconds. follow: a bot that walks back to the runner aims for a ring of its slot's radius times a fresh scale in ring_scale (and its follow_scale), at least min_ring, at most margin inside the follow range. walk_stop: a walking bot stops for hold seconds every gap seconds to chat, looking at the runner or a bot within chat_range. react: a standing bot within range of the runner or a bot that emotes answers after delay seconds with this chance (then waits cool seconds), with an emote from replies (ids in data/player/emotes.json).
